status: Default-off ground experiment; numerical/addressing evidence, not visual or performance acceptance
scope: Canonical local height reference for shared bounded material demand; capability-resolved quality-tier anisotropy and bounded elliptical regular-raster page selection. No physics, displacement, new texture source, cache budget or render pass.
hardware: AMD Radeon 880M Graphics / Vulkan / RADV / Mesa 26.2.5-arch1.1

policy.unknown_or_unsupported: 1x with a fallback note; no vendor/OS inference
policy.disabled_or_conforming: 1x, legacy datum demand, no additional source work
policy.demand: Canonical field height at eye direction, fixed 32 m wavelength; cached per selection epoch/pixel-angle invalidation. Shared by refinement distance, frustum and admission, not exact per-tile terrain or collision height.
policy.filter: max(minor singular value, major singular value / resolved anisotropy); old conservative footprint retained for coverage/globe transitions
policy.budgets: 512 demand leaves and existing source/worker/GPU-layer limits unchanged
policy.legacy_host: Bevy reports anisotropy capability unknown: native sampler policy is not silently claimed there

oracles.cpu: Standing synthetic fixtures at -1000/0/+1000 m reach L22 within 512 leaves with exact area preservation; legacy datum fixture remains L17 away from datum. Cache invalidation and disabled behavior pinned.
oracles.gpu_metric: 864 cases, four channels: conservative and 1/4/16x metrics. Independent f64 finite-difference cube projection plus Gram eigenvalues; absolute error <=1e-6 m + 2e-6 * reference, unchanged tolerance.
oracles.gpu_raster: Production regular raster, grazing eye: red ancestor and blue fine page. Isotropic selects red, 16x selects blue, both retain opaque terrain coverage. Not texture-fidelity or motion acceptance.
oracles.resolver: Enabled/disabled, quality tiers, known/unknown/unsupported capability, conforming fallback, metadata and old serialized settings missing the new field

negative_attempts.failure: Millimetre-scale squared cross products underflowed on the real GPU; normalized metric before computing its area, without weakening tolerance
Legacy host capability literal missed the new field; explicit unknown capability added

Initial isolation capture script matched [shadows] inside a comment rather than a TOML section; assertion stopped before launching a capture. Replaced with anchored section parsing plus parsed-value assertions.

local_evidence: target/surface-showcase/ground-filtering/checks.json and <name>.log; evidence-components.json includes per-log, per-source and frame SHA256s; capture-commands.json contains complete replay commands

captures.replay: binary --graphics settings + common_arguments + --survey-distance 80 --survey-eye-agl 2|50 (overview: 1800/800) --headless output.png --perf-capture output.json; 1280x720, 30 warmup frames
captures.controls: Standing pair matches all native_survey_* metadata; all four captures retain 222 plant descriptors, three draws and 14784 upload bytes, with zero final height/material jobs and zero material misses
captures.cost_limit: One fresh standing pair only; close/overview are candidate diagnostics, not fresh paired timings. Historical WORLD06f frames are separately preserved. No stable speedup claim.
captures.visual_limit: Foreground remains a flat optical proxy; distant horizontal banding, thin-leaf aliasing, coarse mesh shadows, sparse understory and incomplete shore composition remain. More resident texels are not visual acceptance.
captures.blind_review: One shuffled standing pair under review, separate key under private; zero votes
captures.isolation_commands: isolation-commands.json; parsed TOML changes exactly one setting each

isolation.name: no-shadows
isolation.observation: Horizontal ground bands remain, while trunk self-shadow stripes disappear

isolation.name: no-normals
isolation.observation: Distant horizontal ground bands disappear, while coarse/trunk shadows remain; identifies normal-map response as a separate problem, not fixed by shadow resolution

remaining: Seam and moving-camera tests for anisotropic pages
